note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Max attention logit growth in large-batch training motivates MERIT's max-norm, element-wise trust ratio, which yields better large-batch results

nodes.name: Large batches degrade AdamW
nodes.description: Training language models with AdamW at large batch size shows clear performance degradation, requiring additional training tokens to reach comparable generalization.

nodes.name: Max attention logit grows sharply
nodes.description: During large-batch training with AdamW the max attention logit in attention layers increases sharply, exceeding values seen in small-batch training.

nodes.name: Inflated logits hurt attention
nodes.description: An inflated max attention logit yields overly sharp (near one-hot) attention distributions that limit the expressive ability of attention layers.

nodes.name: LAMB reduces only first-layer logit
nodes.description: LAMB's weight-wise trust ratio reduces max attention logit in the first self-attention layer of GPT-2 but not in the medium (12th) layer.

nodes.name: l2 trust ratio ineffective on extremes
nodes.description: There is a large disparity between max norms and l2 norms of query/key weights, so l2-norm-based trust ratios cannot effectively limit the maximum of W_Q/W_K.

nodes.name: Max-norm trust ratio
nodes.description: MERIT computes the trust ratio with the max-norm, giving larger updates to extreme weight values and limiting spikes in max attention logit.

nodes.name: Weights similar within rows/columns
nodes.description: Query/key weight values show high similarity within rows (multi-head attention) and within columns (outlier dimension phenomenon).

nodes.name: Weight-wise ratio is error-prone
nodes.description: LAMB's weight-wise trust ratio is inaccurate because extreme values in one row/column can harm training stability of other rows/columns.

nodes.name: Element-wise ratio design
nodes.description: MERIT computes row-wise and column-wise max-norm ratios and sets the element-wise ratio to the max of them, bounded below by the weight-wise ratio, with element-wise update clipping to 1.

nodes.name: MERIT fixes middle-layer logit growth
nodes.description: MERIT's design successfully suppresses the rapid increase of max attention logit in the middle self-attention layers where LAMB fails.

nodes.name: MERIT beats baselines on val loss
nodes.description: On OpenWebText with GPT-2 small/medium/large, MERIT achieves lower validation loss than LAMB, AdamW, Lion and Sophia-G, with gaps widening as model size grows.

nodes.name: Larger batches without degradation
nodes.description: MERIT enables a 6k batch size with no degradation versus the standard batch size (480) at 48B training tokens, allowing larger batches than LAMB and AdamW.

nodes.name: Ablation: maxLAMB and MERIT loss
nodes.description: Validation loss (GPT-2 small/medium): AdamW 3.470/3.172, LAMB 3.355/3.068, maxLAMB 3.304/3.040, MERIT 3.280/2.982.

nodes.name: Clipping and weight-wise bound matter
nodes.description: Removing element-wise clipping weakens MERIT's gains, and using the weight-wise ratio as a lower bound significantly improves generalization.

isolated_nodes.name: Negligible overhead
isolated_nodes.description: Max-norm and element-wise trust ratio calculation adds about 1% extra computation over LAMB's l2 trust ratio (Table 2).

isolated_nodes.name: QK-Norm hurts large-batch training
isolated_nodes.description: QK-Norm permits larger learning rates for AdamW in GPT-2 but degrades performance in large-batch training (Fig 8).

isolated_nodes.name: Large-batch generalization gap
isolated_nodes.description: Naively increasing batch size degrades generalization (the generalization gap), and Chinchilla-scaled settings used batch 1K/4K/8K for small/medium/large GPT-2.

structural_reasoning: Problem (large-batch degradation, logit growth) leads to diagnosis of LAMB's limits, to MERIT's two design parts, then to empirical results and ablations.
